items.fromString:
*Main Description for Phase1:*

# *Edit POD* permission should be separated to two permissions - *Edit POD in current version* (User will be able to edit POD only in current version) and *Edit POD in new version* (User will be able to edit POD only in a new version). If a user has both permissions should be able to edit POD in the current or in a new version.
# *Edit Customer* permission should be separated to two permissions - *Edit Customer in current version* (User will be able to edit Customer only in current version) and *Edit Customer in new version* (User will be able to edit Customer only in a new version). If a user has both permissions should be able to edit Customer in the current or in a new version.
# A new user permission should be created: *Edit locked Pod in current version*. User should be able to edit locked POD in current version and change only the following fields:
## Name of point of delivery
## Estimated monthly average consumption/production in kWh
## Type of user
# A new user permission should be created: *Edit locked Customer in current version*. User should be able to edit locked Customer in current version and change only the following fields:
## Preferred communication in English
## Form of ownership
## Economic branch based on commercial information
## Economic branch according to the National Classificator
## Main subject of Activity
## Headquarters and address of management
## Additional information
## Managers
## Owners(Partners)
## Communication Data - *only adding new Communication Data. Not able to edit or delete existing Communication Data*

----

*Additional Logic for Phase2:*

No

content.text: Dobromir, should we entirely remove Customer Edit and POD Edit permissions and substitute them with new premissions?
if yes, will you apply those new permissions to users yourself?
Hello, When I was testing this change, I was informed by the analyst that users would never have both

permissions assigned at the same time. I was also informed that this scenario was not covered from a business perspective. Based on that information, I did not consider it a defect or raise a bug for it, as it was outside the expected business use cases.
Hello, we discussed it with Dobromir and it should be possible to set both the permissions together.
If the object is not locked, the user should be able to edit all the fields
If the object is locked, the user should be able to edit only the fields specified in the description (for permission
Hello again, could you please register feedback about this topic?
